status: inactive private firmware reference, not filesystem integration or runtime acceptance
readme: Inactive ASUS firmware reference payload for the BE19000AI BCM side. These packages preserve exact file contents from the pinned, previously reviewed kernel9-ui1 SquashFS. They do not run under Ubuntu, supply compatible shared-library closures, install services, activate scripts, manage hardware, or provide a flashable image. Every stored content file has mode 0644. Original file modes, root ownership, directories and symlink targets are recorded in manifests; original symlinks are never created, so absolute/runtime aliases cannot escape the private versioned namespace. No /sbin/init, /etc, /www, loader, Ubuntu package file or live path is replaced. Kernel modules and runtime state are excluded and fully accounted. The known x86-64 libexpat.so anomaly is excluded. Existing compiler/library binaries stay their original ELF architecture; scripts/resources and metadata belong to Architecture: all. Manufacturer factory/default cryptographic material embedded in the original offline firmware is retained byte-identically for private reference and recorded by path/hash only; no live device keys, NVRAM or credentials were read. Do not activate factory TLS material as unique device credentials. Original component licenses remain in force; this local reference packaging does not grant redistribution rights, and no package is published. Architecture-specific vendor libraries, especially old GLIBC_PRIVATE consumers, still require tested adaptation before Ubuntu use.
limitations: Inactive payload only: no ASUS service has been started or accepted under Ubuntu by this packaging step.
Source metadata roundtrip does not mean a runnable rootfs; symlinks and executable modes remain serialized metadata.
Future integration must assign real multiarch paths and libraries, reconcile usrmerge collisions, and adapt ASUS rc/PID1 ownership through explicit packages.
Old armel glibc/libcrypt/private symbol compatibility, time64 boundaries and native tool roles require independent loader/runtime validation.
Every dynamic executable/plugin dependency, broker/control action and hardware feature must pass acceptance before flashing.
No host installation, device access, publishing, flash, partition change or boot state update is performed.
